exposure: mode of birth (vaginal delivery or cesarean section)
cohort: The study included 89 women aged 16-45 years who had a history of spontaneous and symptomatic cervical artery dissection (CAD) and were admitted between 2005 and 2017.
finding: No cervical artery dissection (CAD) recurrences were observed during subsequent pregnancies or postpartum, irrespective of the type of delivery, suggesting that pregnancy after a history of CAD appears to be safe.
mod_finding: No CAD recurrences were found during subsequent pregnancies or postpartum, irrespective of whether the delivery was vaginal or via cesarean section.
